changes.action: Replace the unconditional fake with temporary SQLite.
changes.details: Apply the real migrations and point the endpoint at the same temporary database. Seed two records with different filter values and distinguishable identifiers. Keep both present for every request.

changes.action: Assert the complete result for each filter value.
changes.details: Request each seeded value through the endpoint and assert that only its corresponding record is returned. Request an unseeded value and assert the endpoint's specified no-match response. Remove SQL substring assertions whose only purpose was to check this filtering behavior.

retained_contracts: Each supported lookup in these cases returns exactly its matching record, excludes the other record, and preserves the endpoint's response shape.
An unmatched lookup preserves the endpoint's existing no-match behavior.
validation: As a one-time check, temporarily make the WHERE condition always true and run the focused endpoint suite. Confirm it fails on a response assertion because an unrelated record is returned.
Restore the predicate and rerun the focused suite against a fresh migrated database. Confirm both matched lookups and the unmatched lookup pass.
cost_and_stop: Each focused run takes about six seconds. Stop after the one-time failure check and passing restored run. Use the existing test lane and endpoint API.
rationale: A SQL substring can survive a broken predicate, and the fake supplies the same rows either way. Two records in the same database make a filtering error observable through the endpoint.
